B: Hiya! Oh, at last, Kerry! I've been hearing about you all afternoon.
A: Erm, hi. Have you? Oh no. What have they said?
B: All good, love, don't worry! Dean said you were sound, and that's high praise from him, I reckon. He's not one for gushing, is he.
A: Ha. No. He was alright though. Once you got him going.
B: That's what I thought! I'm Leanne, Castleford, West Yorkshire. And you're Lowestoft, same as Matthew's mum and dad?
A: Yeah. Marisol said he's from there. I didn't know. I haven't had him yet.
B: Oh, he's lovely, you'll like him. Bit shy. So what is it you do, or, sorry, have you been asked that a hundred times?
A: Erm, a few times. I'm not working at the minute. I was a picker in a warehouse, they cut the shifts, so I'm looking. Cleaning or warehouse, early shifts. Is that alright?
B: Course it is. I'm on a packing line, food factory, so not a million miles off. I train the new starters. Honestly, the agency lot I get, if they turned up on time and didn't put their hairnet on their chin, I'd be made up. That's all anyone wants.
A: That's what Marisol said. She said quiet and reliable is gold.
B: She's right. You'd be fine, you. You've got that look, like you'd just crack on.
A: Ha. Thanks. I get nervous in interviews though. I sort of go blank.
B: Oh, me too. Me too. I was signed off with stress a few years back and going back in, I were shaking. But you get through it. You do.
A: Yeah.
B: Sorry, that got a bit heavy. What do you do of an evening? What are you watching?
A: Erm, Married at First Sight. True crime stuff. Old Gavin and Stacey. It's a bit, erm, I watch a lot of telly on my own, do you know what I mean.
B: Oh, I know exactly what you mean. I'm on my own too, just me and Mavis, my cat. Some nights it's lovely and some nights it's just quiet, isn't it. Too quiet. That's why I do choir and Zumba, to get me out.
A: Marisol said I should go back to Zumba. I used to go with my friend but she moved away.
B: You should! Go on, go to one. Stand at the back. Nobody's looking, I promise you, they're all looking at themselves in the mirror. I'm at the front now and I were at the back for a year.
A: Were you? Ha. Okay. Maybe.
B: And true crime! I read them books and then I can't sleep. I'm checking the back door twice.
A: Oh, me too. I listened to a podcast, the whole series in one go, and then I heard a noise and it was just the radiator.
B: Ha! It's always the radiator! Or the cat. Mavis knocked a glass off once at two in the morning and I was stood there with the hoover pipe.
A: The hoover pipe?
B: It were the nearest thing!
A: That's quite funny actually.
